title: Bonded labour rehabilitation - the remedies that exist only on paper
p1: A person is rescued from bonded labour. The law promises freedom, support, and a fresh start. But what happens after the rescue often decides whether justice is real or just paperwork.
p2: Many people assume that ending bonded labour means the problem is solved. The surprising reality is that rehabilitation is where the biggest gaps appear. A release certificate, financial assistance, and support schemes may exist, but delays, lack of awareness, and poor implementation can leave survivors struggling to rebuild their lives.
p3: Bonded labour rehabilitation is not only about freeing someone from exploitation. It is about helping them regain independence through timely support, livelihood opportunities, and protection from being trapped again. A remedy written in a law book has little value if it never reaches the person who needs it.
